title: Researched And ‘Observated’ To Death In The Barle Valley
content:
Stag chased to exhaustion and killed as the hunt invoked bogus exemptions when caught on camera.




WATCH THE VIDEO (VIEWER DISCRETION ADVISED)







The stag was pursued for hours. Credit North Dorset Hunt Sabs




On 17 October 2026, a North Dorset Hunt Saboteur witnessed the final moments of a stag pursued for hours through the Barle Valley before being shot in Marsh Wood. The stag was barely able to walk, his mouth wide open and tongue hanging out, with hounds and a gunman following behind.




Gunman James Wyatt following the stag, who by now was barely able to walk. Credit North Dorset Hunt Sabs




After they shot him, the excuses began.




Predictably, the focus turned to why the sab was there, rather than what they had just done to the animal. Perhaps the stress of having a sab witness their cruelty, made the hunters forget their well-rehearsed lines.




Wyatt was upset that his cruelty was being filmed. Credit: North Dorset Hunt Sabs.




This hunt hides behind the ‘Research and Observation’ smokescreen, but it is clearly a ruse, and the hunt even made up its own word to justify its cruelty.

‘observated’

 the stag. It’s not even a real word.

author: webadmin
title: Where Is The Hunting Ban, Labour?
content:
This fox was illegally hunted at a joint meet of the North Cotswold Hunt and the Warwickshire Hunt on Saturday 14th November. Image credit: West Midlands Hunt Sabs




In July 2024, the Labour Government made a manifesto commitment to ban trail hunting and improve the Hunting Act.




On 26 March 2026, the Government launched a consultation to determine how best to implement an effective and enforceable ban on trail hunting in England and Wales.




The consultation closed on 18 June, having received 184,000 responses. Yet months later, we are still waiting for the results and a clear timetable for what happens next.




The Government has acknowledged the risks trail hunting poses to wildlife, including the danger of hounds pursuing and killing live animals. It has also recognised concerns that trail hunting can be used as a smokescreen for illegal hunting.
















This fox was hunted and killed by the Blackmore and Sparkford Vale (BSV) Hunt on Thursday 19th November. Image credit: Locals Against The BSV Hunt




Meanwhile, wildlife continues to suffer.




Foxes and other wild animals are chased, injured and killed. Our local hunt saboteur groups are out week after week, witnessing and documenting incidents and working to protect wildlife, often with little support.

title: Quorn Hunt Humiliated: Terrierman Arrested As Sabs Disrupt Opening Meet.
content:
Legendary animal liberationist Barry Horne honoured by Northants Sabs.




Just weeks after publishing damning footage of the 

Quorn Hunt killing a fox and training hounds

 to attack, saboteurs descended upon their prestigious opening meet – and completely ruined it.




Quorn Killers and Horne Haunts Quorn. Banners proudly displayed by Northants Sabs at the Quorn killers opening meet, 6 November, 2026. Image: Northants Hunt Sabs.




The day saw violence and abuse by the hunt, and resulted in the arrest of a terrierman who attempted to flee from police.




The day was dedicated to Barry Horne, a legendary activist who made the ultimate sacrifice for animal liberation.




Barry was involved in numerous daring rescue operations, helping to free animals destined for experimentation. He died following a series of hunger strikes intended to pressure Tony Blair’s Labour government over its promise to hold an inquiry into vivisection.




Barry Horne, 17 March 1990, rescuing 82 beagle puppies and 26 rabbits from Harlan Interfauna in Huntingdon. The site is now associated with MBR Acres Ltd, and the long-running Camp Beagle protests against the breeding of dogs for laboratory experiments for the petrochemical, chemical and pharmaceutical industries.

title: A Licence to Hunt: “Cruel, Inhumane and Selfish” Lauderdale Huntswoman Sentenced: 300 Hours’ Unpaid Work and Ten-Year Dog Ban
content:
Scotland’s first conviction under the Hunting with Dogs (Scotland) Act 2023 has resulted in a substantial community sentence for ex-huntswoman Claire Bellamy, following evidence gathered by Glasgow Hunt Saboteurs.




Claire Bellamy after breaching the licence. 

Image: Glasgow Hunt Sabs.




Former Lauderdale Hunt master and huntswoman Claire Bellamy has been sentenced to 300 hours of unpaid work and banned from owning or keeping most dogs for ten years after being convicted of deliberately hunting a fox with hounds. 




Bellamy appeared at Paisley Sheriff Court on Monday 9th November, where Sheriff Gill imposed the maximum 300 hours of unpaid work permitted under a Community Payback Order, to be completed within 12 months. 




The sentence follows 

Bellamy’s conviction in October

, the first secured under Scotland’s Hunting with Dogs (Scotland) Act 2023.




The prosecution was made possible thanks to footage captured by Glasgow Hunt Saboteurs, who have been documenting the ongoing illegal hunting in Scotland that has continued since the new licensing system became law. 




On the 4th January 2025 – almost 2 years after the new law came into force – Bellamy was hunting with approximately 17 hounds near Kirkton Woods, between Houston in Renfrewshire and Kilmacolm in Inverclyde.

title: THIS IS FOX HUNTING
content:
The main fox hunting season is now in full swing all over the country and already hunts are doing everything they can to prove to the general public and the government why a full ban on hunting with hounds is needed now. Meanwhile their governing body, the British Hound Sports Association (BHSA) are sitting back and allowing the pro hunt community to destroy themselves.










The video above is from the opening meet of the Warwickshire Hunt on the 31

st

 of October 2026 and shows them blatantly hunting a fox. This is just one example, but make no mistake this is happening all over the country week in and week out. 




A fox is shown fleeing from a covert on the Upton Estate, which sits on the border of Oxfordshire and Warwickshire. Moments later hounds are in cry pursuing the fox towards a covert named Shenington Hirons while a young rider is seen tracking the hounds as they hunt the fox, which then attempts to seek refuge in a hedgerow.




A West Midlands Hunt Saboteur is heard informing other sabs that hounds are marking in a hedgerow. The same young rider who was previously seen tracking hounds is sat watching, knowing full well that hounds are indicating they have located a fox. title: SAVE THE SOUTH SUFFOLK ONE!
content:
Oh, wait… sorry. The Judge already did that in court. 




John ‘Pinocchio’ Henty’s case ends in acquittal

. 




Thank you to

 

South Suffolk Hunt Sabs

 

for this guest article.




A court case brought by former Essex & Suffolk Hunt huntsman John Henty against a hunt saboteur has ended in a resounding victory for the defence, with the saboteur found NOT GUILTY.




John Henty outside court.




Following allegations made to police, former Essex & Suffolk Hunt huntsman John Henty pursued a prosecution alleging abusive and threatening behaviour under Section 5 of the Public Order Act. The case followed an incident on a quiet country lane in which Henty pursued the hunt saboteurs’ vehicle, blocked it in, approached it and attempted to provoke a reaction.




What followed was a lengthy legal process based on Henty’s account of events. However, when his evidence was examined in court, serious questions arose about the credibility of that account and whether the alleged behaviour actually amounted to a criminal offence.




A case that should never have reached court?




The Judge was highly critical of the way the case had been handled by the CPS and the police officers involved, making clear that the alleged actions did not meet the legal threshold required for a criminal offence.

title: No Land, No Hunting
content:
Thank you to West Midlands Hunt Saboteurs for this guest article.




On Thursday 8th October, West Midlands Hunt Sabs (WMHS) held a protest outside The Bower House in Shipston on Stour. The restaurant is owned by Andrew Stephen Bower Knight, who continually allows, not only the Warwickshire Hunt to illegally hunt foxes on his land at Compton Scorpion, but the North Cotswold Hunt too.




The protest caused quite a stir amongst the pro-hunt community prompting the British Hound Sports Association (BHSA) to publish a social media post stating 

“Rural businesses are under attack by urban saboteurs.”




Visitors to The Bower House in Shipston on Stour were made aware that business owner, Andrew Stephen Bower Knight, enables illegal fox hunting.




The campaign against the Warwickshire Hunt is one that spans back years and is steeped in controversy, including the fact that Warwickshire Police entered into a “secret deal” with the hunt when they withdrew the Community Protection Notice that they had been issued.




WMHS have always highlighted the importance of holding landowners to account, something which featured heavily in the campaign against the now defunct Atherstone Hunt. The Hunting Act stipulates that should a landowner allow the hunting of a wild mammal with dogs on their land then they are breaking the law.
